newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FEATURE - Frenchman hopes to scale world's tallest building.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Frenchman hopes to scale world's tallest building.

text.p: Frenchman Alain Robert says movie musclemen Arnold Schwarzenegger and Sylvester Stallone would probably balk at doing what he does for a living.

Known as "Spiderman", Robert climbs tall buildings and steep towers as a profession. He is in Malaysia hoping to scale the world's tallest twin buildings, the 452-metre (1,483 feet) Petronas Twin Towers. He thinks he can scamper up the side of the building in 90 minutes.
"If you're Schwarzenegger you can do nothing, just look at the building. If you're Stallone, you can do nothing," he told Reuters in an interview.
A sinewy 1.64 metres (5 feet 5 inches) and 48 kg (106 pounds), he said the big bulk of the action movie stars is a disadvantage when climbing buildings.
Robert, 34, has climbed about 30 structures around the world often using little more than his hands and earning him names such as "Spiderman", "Madman", "Human Fly" and "Big Little Man".
On Friday, Spiderman practiced for his planned assault on the twin towers by climbing the 76.2-metre (250 feet) Kuala Lumpur hotel he was staying in within 10 minutes.
Robert nearly made it to the peak of the Petronas Towers on March 20, climbing to the 60th floor of the steel and glass building, before waiting police hauled him off.
He was jailed for a couple of days before being released.
But a Malaysia youth group, apparently with a nod from Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, wants him to have a go at the towers again, this time for charity.
One of the beneficiaries of the fund-raiser would be the Malaysian AIDS foundation, chaired by the prime minister's daughter, Marina Mahathir.
Robert has one more barrier to overcome before he can tackle the building -- the authorities who manage the towers and its surrounding office park, the Kuala Lumpur City Centre.
They have withheld permission so far, saying they are worried about damage to the building.

Robert made world headlines last month when he was arrested climbing the Sydney Tower in Australia, armed with only chalk powder, three ropes, some masking tape and a karabiner (a spring-loaded metal clip designed for joining ropes together).
Among structures he has climbed since 1994 are New York's Empire State Building, London's Canary Wharf and the Far East Finance Centre in Hong Kong.
"All over the world, I bring a part of dream for them. For them climbing is incredible because the people are afraid to fall," Robert said.
During the interview on the ground floor of a busy Kuala Lumpur building, Malaysians came up to shake his hand, ask for autographs and even shout out his nickname.
Girls smiled and giggled shyly as they walked past, waving their hands.
A few motorists honked their car horns. "Go for it Spiderman!" said one. "You're a hero," said another.
Said Robert: "There is a cartoon Spiderman. But I am the real Spiderman."
He started out as a mountain and rock climber in 1975, before taking on tall buildings as a different challenge.
"I am very proud of what I do because I realised my dream. My dream is to climb and if I can (get) money with my dream, it's fantastic," he said.
Married to 36-year old Nicole, with three boys aged nine, six and two, he said his wife is not exactly thrilled with his profession. "All the wives will be afraid. It's normal."
He said it was possible to climb 80 percent of all buildings, although he accepts there are risks to the job.
"I need a small edge. I am not a bird, I am not god. I need a small edge to hold."
"Before I climb, I am like everybody. I'm scared to fall and to die...I accept the risk, I know exactly what can happen."
